newsitem.title: USA: Northland Cranberries is sued over crop.
newsitem.headline: Northland Cranberries is sued over crop.

text.p: Northland Cranberries Inc has been sued by Ocean Spray Cranberries Inc, a growers' cooperative, over a portion of the 1996 cranberry crop, Northland said Monday.

The suit, filed September 6 in Wisconsin Circuit Court, seeks an order requiring Northland, Koller Cranberry Co of Manitowish Waters, Wis., and certain Koller affiliates to deliver to Ocean Spray the cranberry crop from 74 planted acres, Northland said.
The 74 acres were acquired by Northland from Koller in July.
The suit also seeks to enjoin Northland from alleged interference with any of the cooperative marketing agreements that Ocean Spray maintains with its growers.

Northland said Ocean Spray entered into a cooperative marketing agreement with Koller in 1992. The agreement states that for each barrel of cranberries from the Koller property not delivered to Ocean Spray, the cooperative is entitled to payment equal to 50 percent of the average total price per barrel paid by Ocean Spray for three prior annual crops.
Northland said it believes Wisconsin law imposes a limit on such payment of 30 percent of the average proceeds.
The average proceeds per barrel for the three prior cranberry crops was about $56. Thirty percent of this amount is about $17.
Northland said the average crop from the Koller property over the prior three years was about 12,850 barrels.

Northland said it recently settled a similar dispute with Ocean Spray regarding Northland's acquisition of cranberry marshes from Yellow River Cranberry Co. Under that settlement, Northland paid Ocean Spray an amount equal to 30 percent of the average proceeds per barrel for the cranberries not delivered to Ocean Spray.
